body:
Part of #50. Stacked on #75; the base becomes `main` once #75 merges.

The first step of the whole-batch write path from the [design change on #50](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/50): requests cross from a client connection to the committer, and replies come back, as batches instead of one at a time.

- **Admission.** The connection reader decodes every complete unary request the node runs (KV, Compact, and the unary Lease calls). It hands them to the node with one `Node.SubmitBatch` call when the next frame is not fully buffered yet, or at 256 requests or 4 MiB. There is no timer: a lone request goes out at once.
- **Completion.** After each `Process`, the committer groups the replies by connection and calls `Complete` once per connection with all of them. `Complete` only appends to the connection's queue and wakes its writer; the writer encodes the replies.
- **Gone from this path:** the goroutine, the context, the `request` struct and the reply channel per call, and the inbox send per call. A call the node runs now has no context of its own. The client enforces its `grpc-timeout`, the node's 7 s request timeout still applies, and a reset drops the reply.
- **Bounds.** A connection may have 64 MiB of request bytes unanswered by the node. Above that, its reader stops reading until replies come back. If the node stops, the writer fails every call the node still holds with "server stopped".
- `Node.Do` stays for `/health`, the keepalive stream and the rare calls (Status, MemberList).

Not in this PR: decoding values in wire form, encoding the entry once and applying it in place, and the allocation strategy experiment. Those are the next PRs.

Tests: the new `TestNodeStopsUnderLoad` stops a node while 50 calls wait on it, and every call must get an answer. The existing server tests and the #75 frontend tests pass with `-race`.
title: Whole-batch admission and grouped completion between connections and the committer
